key_insight: Mixing nanoscale Laponite with microscale Bentonite reduces drying damage, with most intermediate compositions on glass outperforming a simple average of the pure-clay outcomes.
engineering_relevance: Clay composition offers a practical route to improve crack resistance in coatings, barrier layers and ceramic processing.
method: Compared drying damage across clay compositions on hydrophobic polypropylene and hydrophilic glass.
Measured two-step yielding in gelled suspensions and derived cohesive energies.
Used an energy-balance-based cohesion–adhesion index to interpret peeling versus cracking.
evidence_signal: Replicate experiments supported essentially intact Laponite films, extensively fractured Bentonite films and reduced damage in mixtures; every composition exhibited two-step yielding.
watch_item: Rheology–cracking correlations must specify the yielding step used because derived cohesive energies differ by orders of magnitude.
paper_title: Resisting Drying Stress in Laponite Bentonite Clay Composites, Two Step Yielding and Crack Peel Selection
